summary: Iteration 3 (Emergent Google Auth). Backend: 9/9 pytest tests passed covering: (1) POST /api/auth/google/session returns 400 'X-Session-ID header ausente' when header missing; (2) returns 401 'session_id inválido ou expirado' when Emergent returns non-200 for an invalid session_id (verified against real Emergent endpoint); (3) legacy JWT login admin@locafacil.com.br + /auth/me still works with access_token cookie; (4) cookie precedence — with BOTH access_token (admin JWT) and session_token (points to Google user) set, /auth/me resolves the Google user via session_token (session_token wins); (5) session expiry — expired session in db.sessions falls back to JWT, returning 401 when no JWT present; (6) logout deletes the session document from db.sessions and clears both cookies (subsequent /auth/me → 401); (7) admin elevation logic for tailansantos06@gmail.com verified via db simulation for both first-login create (role='admin', kyc_level='approved', auth_provider='google', password_hash='', avatar from picture, social fields defaulted '') and existing-user elevation ($set role='admin', kyc_level='approved'); (8) session upsert (same session_token twice → 1 document). Frontend: /login shows google-auth-btn labeled 'Entrar com Google'; /cadastro shows google-auth-btn labeled 'Criar conta com Google'; both correctly redirect to https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=<encoded origin>/auth-callback (verified by intercepting the top-level nav — URL = 'https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Faluguel-veiculos-br.preview.emergentagent.com%2Fauth-callback'). /auth-callback direct nav (no hash) redirects to /login. Hash detection verified end-to-end: visiting /buscar#session_id=fake_capture triggers Shell to render <AuthCallback/>, which calls POST /api/auth/google/session with X-Session-ID header, receives 401, toasts 'session_id inválido ou expirado', and navigates to /login. Full integration path proven live.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 1133 lines — split into routers/ (auth.py, bookings.py, vehicles.py, admin.py) — recurring recommendation from iter1/iter2, still not addressed.
get_current_user (server.py:85-126) correctly checks session_token cookie first, then Authorization Bearer session match, then falls back to JWT access_token cookie — precedence order matches spec.
Session expiry check (server.py:99-104) is timezone-safe: parses ISO strings, patches naive datetimes to UTC before comparing — good.

POST /api/auth/google/session (server.py:313-377) uses upsert with session_token as the unique key — no duplicates possible. Also correctly elevates existing users whose email is in ADMIN_GOOGLE_EMAILS (server.py:362-364).
ADMIN_GOOGLE_EMAILS is a hardcoded Python set of size 1 — acceptable for single-owner platform, but consider moving to env var for future flexibility (e.g. ADMIN_EMAILS='a@b.com,c@d.com').

AuthCallback.jsx uses useRef guard against React 18 StrictMode double-mount → good. Reads location.hash reactively via useLocation — Shell in App.js also reads it synchronously to render callback on any route with #session_id=.
AuthContext skips /auth/me GET when hash contains 'session_id=' — prevents an initial 401 before the callback stores the cookie.
GoogleAuthButton constructs redirect from window.location.origin (no hardcoding). Both callers pass different labels — clean.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all 6 spec items verified: login btn, register btn, redirect URL construction on both pages, /auth-callback no-hash fallback, hash detection reactive rendering, end-to-end 401 error surfacing)
